findings.summary: D125 should say it amends D24's 'every push' trigger, and should note that the matching text in athena-v0.md is now stale.
findings.evidence: docs/decisions.md line 588-590, D24: "`ci.yml` runs on every push and pull request, and weekly." docs/design/athena-v0.md lines 1016 and 1436 say the same. After this change those lines are out of date. D24 cannot be edited because of the D122 hash pin, and athena-v0.md is not in the request's file list. Fix: Have D125 say that it amends D24's trigger clause. Note in D125, or under open questions, that the athena-v0.md §11.2 wording ('every push') is now stale and is left for a follow-up, since that file is out of scope.

findings.summary: The early_run_wait open question can be closed now: run lookups do not filter by event.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs:885-893: `ci_runs` queries `actions/runs?head_sha={commit}` with no event filter. `check_run` (895-899) reads `commits/{commit}/check-runs` by job name. Neither needs a push run, so after the change they just see one run instead of two. Fix: Close the open question with this evidence, and keep Step 1 as a quick confirmation. No Rust change is needed.

findings.summary: D125 should say that athena/records is no longer scanned on push.
findings.evidence: With push limited to main, the history job (gitleaks over all commits, D24) runs on non-main branches only through pull_request, workflow_dispatch or the weekly schedule. That includes athena/records, which never gets a pull request. Fix: Have D125 say so explicitly: after this change, athena/records is scanned only when a run is started by hand (workflow_dispatch). The weekly cron runs on the default branch, so it does not scan athena/records either.

summary: The plan matches the request and the accepted reading. I read the snapshot: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 15 has a bare `push:`, lines 16-20 keep pull_request, workflow_dispatch and the cron, and the job name on line 27 is 'fmt, clippy, tests'. The latest decision is D124 (docs/decisions.md:3085), so D125 is the right number, and appending only is right given the D122 hash pin. The header comment on lines 1-11 stays accurate. Its claim that only a default-branch push saves the shared caches still holds once push is limited to main. The plan's main open risk, that landing might depend on push runs, is answered by gh.rs: `ci_runs` queries by head_sha with no event filter, and the required check is looked up by job name, so one pull_request run is enough. The demonstrations fit content criteria: they are diff reads, plus cargo test and clippy for criterion 6. The post-landing criterion is correctly recorded as a follow-up rather than claimed. The work is small and fits one producer run. The findings are minor: D125 should say it amends D24's "every push" trigger and that athena-v0.md is now stale, and it should state that athena/records loses push-run scanning.
